messages:
alex: quick follow-up to the provenance handshake RFC — i pushed a pared-down proposal that avoids shipping full envelopes on every event. TL;DR: keep a tiny pointer + checksum, and only materialize provenance for audit/backfill flows.
maria: link? want to read the diff.
alex: https://docs.internal/rfc/provenance-slimdown — main change is `token_provenance_ref` instead of full `provenance_body`. tiny JSON: {"ref": "p-<fingerprint>", "crc": "abc123" }
raj: curious about tradeoffs. if we only store a ref on the ingest path, how do we guarantee availability for later audits? replication / GC concerns.
taylor: +1 on availability question. also: what about correctness windows — if ref points to data that gets compacted, audits could fail.
alex: good points. proposal includes a low-retention hot-store (7d) for provenance + a cold-store archive for >7d. the `ref` includes a storage-era tag so we can route fetches.
maria: do we have metrics for how often audits fetch the full provenance? i'd rather avoid a fetch-heavy pattern at query time.
raj: we have rough numbers: ~0.5% of billing events ever trigger a forensic fetch historically. most audits are aggregate-only.
taylor: 0.5% seems fine, but spikes are possible when a tenant disputes an invoice. need SLO for fetch latency.
alex: design idea: fetch path has two levels — first try hot-store (fast), fallback to cold-store async rehydrate. if fallback, return a 202 and kick a background rehydrate job + notify ops.
sre-bot: [alert-sim] simulated 99th fetch latency to hot-store = 120ms, cold-store cold-start = 6s.
raj: that 6s fallback is acceptable for human-driven audits, but not for automated reconciliation that expects sub-second. we should auto-fallback to a compatible cached snapshot for reconcile jobs.
maria: also consider token-level privacy: provenance may contain redacted user content. storing pointers must preserve redaction guarantees.
alex: yep — refs point to an encrypted, redaction-aware payload; decrypt keys are gated by KMS roles. we'll add an attribute `redaction_level` on the ref.
taylor: operationally, how do we GC old provenance without breaking append-only ledger semantics?
raj: idea: keep proof frames (commit hashes) in the ledger forever, but GC full bodies after archive TTL. proofs allow verification of historical charges without full payload.
alex: exactly — keep small verification artifacts with each token event (fingerprint + merkle-proof-root) so you can prove correctness even if body gone. full body only for deep audits.
maria: can you sketch the ingest event schema?
alex: short sketch: `{"event_id":"e..","tenant_id":"t..","usage_tokens":123,"provenance_ref":{"ref":"p-<fp>","crc":"abc123","era":"hot","redaction_level":"partial"},"proof_root":"r.."}`
raj: any change needed in existing handshake where downstream connectors expect full envelope? backward compat?
alex: plan: v1 adapter emits both `provenance_ref` and `provenance_body` for a transition window. config flag to flip per-connector.
taylor: we should add a migration task that scans high-SLA tenants and populates hot-store proactively before flipping. avoids noisy fallbacks.
maria: testing/rollout?
alex: propose experiment: rollout 5% of tenants for 2 weeks, monitor fetch-rate, fetch-latency, and audit-fallout. if <1% increase in reconciles and no missing-provenance incidents, expand. metrics: `provenance.fetch.rate`, `provenance.miss.rate`, `audit.retry.count`.
raj: add a synthetic test that simulates a 1000-tenant audit day to catch scale fail cases.
sre-bot: scheduled job created: `prov-sim-load-1000` starting 1705060000.
deploy-bot: RFC doc published to docs.internal and flagged for product review.
taylor: sounds good. one last note: update billing SLA doc to mention possible 202 for deep-audit payloads. ops must be clear to customers.
alex: will draft the rollout playbook and the billing note. thanks all :thumbsup:
